notes:
Summary: Large developer platform (internal IDE + cloud-hosted plugins) evaluating Redwood for enterprise copilot. Key asks: sub-100ms streaming latency for inline completions, model pinning per engineering org, predictable per-seat cost for budgeting, and audit+retention for regulatory teams.

Highlights from discovery call (2026-02-03):
- "We need costs to be predictable by team — finance will not accept surprise token bursts." — VP Eng.
- Testing profile: ~8k active devs, median session 2–3 minutes, spike windows around deploys and nightly builds.
- Latency target: 40–120ms for inline streaming, 95th percentile <200ms overall.
- Throughput: sustained 450 requests/sec during peak workspace activity; burst to 2k req/sec for large org-wide refactors.
- Cost-sensitivity: high — looking to move away from open but un-optimized fleet that costs more than expected. Caching/prefix reuse & quantization critical.
- Security: SSO (Okta), audit logs ingested into Splunk, per-team data residency in US/EU, retention controls.

Sales notes / negotiation cues:
- POC ask: 90-day pilot focusing on caching layers (prefix/KV caching), token-level cost telemetry and quantization profiles; include A/B with q4_0 vs int8 quant to measure quality delta.
- Wants a clear fallback policy: hosted -> dedicated -> on-prem if cost or latency spikes.
- Procurement asked for seat-based pricing bands for 1k / 5k / 10k active seats plus overage rules.

Quote snippets and friction: 
- "If you can show 60% token reduction via smart caching for our completion patterns, finance signs faster."
- Legal: DPA comments were submitted 2026-02-10; asking for SOC2 + ISA annex to be explicit about audit retention windows.

Action items recorded:
- AE (Avery) to deliver POC design + measurement plan by 2026-02-24.
- SE (Marcus) to draft quantization experiment matrix and expected perf/cost delta.
- Infra (Rajiv) to provide network constraints for VPC peering by 2026-02-28.
- CSM (Samira) to prepare onboarding checklist and seat migration plan.
